title: Cap Automators hold a constant headroom above current usage instead of a fixed exposure ceiling
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.3 replaces static supply and borrow caps with a three-parameter automaton: `gap` — "the target available exposure," `ttl` — "the cooldown period for cap increases," and `max` — "the absolute maximum exposure." Authorized parties "can update a covered Supply Cap or Borrow Cap so the available exposure is equal to the target."

The quantity being held constant is not the cap but the *distance between the cap and actual usage*. A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.3.1.1 defines `gap` as "the target gap between the supply usage and the Supply Cap." As deposits grow, the cap is ratcheted up to keep the same headroom; as they shrink, it comes back down.

This solves a real governance failure. A static cap is either set generously — in which case it does not constrain anything until a sudden inflow fills it all at once — or set tightly, in which case it blocks organic growth and each raise costs a governance cycle. A trailing cap does both jobs: at any instant, no more than `gap` can be added before hitting the ceiling, so a single large deposit or exploit cannot balloon exposure, while steady growth needs no votes at all.

Governance retains only the outer bound. `max` is the number a vote must change; everything inside it is automation. Notably, A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.3.3 lists exactly one authorized party — an address labelled "ALM Proxy **Freezable**" — so the automation is itself a single, haltable component rather than an open permission.
description: gap sets target available exposure, ttl the cooldown on increases, max the absolute ceiling — so caps track adoption automatically while governance retains only the outer bound.
